title: Wedjat eye-first deepening: internal value-mapping permutation control and museum spiral-position canary

research_pivot.question_1: Is the conventional assignment 1/2..1/64 recoverable from the geometry of the six eye-part glyphs themselves?
research_pivot.question_2: Does one directly measurable canonical Wedjat feature—the lower-left spiral/curl—show a reproducible positional change across museum objects through time?
research_pivot.reason: The previous all-hieroglyph control showed that raw resemblance has substantial false-positive pressure. The next useful layer is therefore internal eye structure and diachronic eye morphology, kept separate from CSM sign genealogy.

moller_1911_strong_thesis.source: Georg Möller, Die Zeichen für die Bruchteile des Hohlmasses und das Uzatauge, 1911
moller_1911_strong_thesis.summary: As reconstructed by Ritter, Möller linked CSM signs to parts of the completed right Wedjat using proximity of forms on votive cubits and visual similarity of remaining signs. Möller explicitly acknowledged that parts of the mythological reconstruction were hypothesis.

ritter_2003_correction.source: Jim Ritter, Closing the Eye of Horus: The Rise and Fall of Horus-eye Fractions
established_for_this_registry: Ritter reports that the further back third-millennium hieratic CSM signs are traced, the further they diverge from their supposed Horus-eye counterparts.
Ritter states that no non-metrological use of all D11-D16 eye-part signs is known before the Middle Kingdom at the earliest; on the hieroglyphic side only D11 is relevant that early.
Ritter therefore rejects the strong primordial derivation thesis, while discussing a weaker possibility of later secondary identification as a separate question.

museum_style_anchor.museum_statement_summary: The Met explicitly describes this New Kingdom Wedjat as having the spiral directly under the cosmetic line and contrasts later examples where the spiral is much lower.

test_A_internal_value_mapping_permutatio.method: For each simple geometry metric, fit metric ~= C*fraction in log2 space under the conventional D011..D016 assignment, then exhaustively evaluate all 6! = 720 assignments. A low rank would mean the conventional assignment is unusually recoverable from geometry; a high rank means many alternative assignments fit as well or better.

summary.interpretation: The conventional fraction order is not encoded by simple physical size or skeleton extent in the modern eye-part glyph shapes; for all three primary metrics, most permutations fit at least as well or better.

test_A_internal_value_mapping_permutatio.highest_admissible_claim: The numerical values are not recoverable from simple modern glyph geometry. If a historical eye-part/value association existed, it cannot be justified as a proportional-size code from these shapes.

method.segmentation: Estimate border background in Lab color space, Otsu-threshold color distance, morphology, keep largest connected component.
method.candidate_method: Hough circle candidates in the lower-left ROI scored by the fraction of candidate circumference lying within 3 px of detected object edges.
method.warning: This detector is a loop-like spiral canary, not a semantic recognizer of Egyptian iconography.

chronological_spiral_depth_test.interpretation: Exploratory directional canary only. A larger y means the detected lower-left loop sits lower in the object bounding box.

observed_pattern.early_555588: No candidate crosses the frozen 0.50 support threshold (best support 0.3833).
observed_pattern.direction: Among the four detected post-early examples, spiral y-position increases monotonically from the New Kingdom canary to the Ptolemaic object. Spearman rho=1.0; with only four objects the exact two-sided permutation p is 2/24 = 0.08333, so this is directional and underpowered, not an admission result.

test_B_museum_spiral_position_canary.relation_to_museum_text: The detected direction is consistent with the Met independent description that New Kingdom spirals sit directly below the cosmetic line whereas later examples place the spiral lower.
critical_limitations: Only five local images are used; the frozen primary protocol requires at least 12 candidate objects and at least 8 with all six valid landmarks.
The local bytes were already visually inspected before v0.4 SHA-256 sealing, so this cannot be promoted as a cold preregistered measurement.
Object 551474 is used as an external calibration canary and is not one of the frozen twelve primary objects.
Material, manufacturing technique, image angle and object damage can affect loop detectability and apparent position.
The 555588 non-detection does not prove the spiral was historically absent; it is only a detector result on one early artifact image.

new_eye_first_hypothesis.statement: The canonical visual grammar of the Wedjat—including an explicit lower-left spiral and its standardized placement—may have undergone diachronic canonicalization independently of the older abstract CSM metrological system.
new_eye_first_hypothesis.why_testable: Ritter supplies a paleographic prediction (earlier CSM forms diverge from later eye counterparts) while The Met independently documents a period-dependent shift in spiral placement. The eye-object lane can therefore test visual canonicalization without assuming fraction values.

required_steps: Acquire and SHA-256 seal the exact primary Open Access image bytes for all twelve already-frozen Met objects before new measurements.
Annotate eye morphology without fraction labels: eye outline, distinct pupil/iris, eyebrow/cosmetic line, diagonal falcon mark, spiral terminal, vertical cheek extension.
Measure spiral center y, spiral radius/path length, vertical-tail depth, pupil diameter and eye width with at least two independent annotators.
Test period effects and leave-one-period-group-out stability before comparing any measurement with 1/2..1/64.
Only after the visual grammar is independently characterized, compare its chronology with the separate CSM paleographic chronology.
next_gate.promotion_condition: A temporal morphology result must replicate across independent objects and period groups and survive material/style controls. No fraction or binary meaning follows automatically from eye morphology.

highest_admissible_claim: The conventional 1/2..1/64 assignment is not recoverable from simple geometry of the six modern eye-part glyphs: its mapping ranks 633rd, 659th and 633rd out of 720 for area, bounding-box diagonal and skeleton length. Separately, an exploratory loop detector on five museum-image bytes finds no strong spiral-like loop in the earliest sampled object but detects one in four later objects; among those four, normalized spiral depth moves monotonically downward with chronology, directionally matching The Met description of New Kingdom versus later Wedjat style. Because the museum pilot is small, previously viewed, and not the full preregistered corpus, it establishes a testable eye-canonicalization candidate, not a historical fraction derivation or ancient code.
